decisions.topic: Frontend framework for the local web app
options: Flask + simple HTML pages (no build step)
decisions.choice: Flask + simple HTML pages
decisions.WHY: Tiny, no build step, runs on any OS with one command, easiest for friends to run offline. User explicitly wanted very lightweight (legacy Q1).

decisions.topic: How existing XLSM data migrates into SQLite
decisions.choice: One-time Python import script; XLSM kept as read-only backup
decisions.WHY: Full rebuild agreed: data + Dashboard + status logic all leave Excel; XLSM retired as working tool (legacy Q3).

options: Row-per-payment ledger (bond, month, amount, paid) with UI-rendered month grid
One column per month (Excel-style) in SQLite
decisions.choice: Row-per-payment ledger; totals/status become live queries
decisions.WHY: Fixes hardcoded headers (Sep-2025..Feb-2027), Jan-2031 scan limit, and stale dashboard. Scales as portfolio grows.

decisions.topic: CSV/Excel export once Excel is no longer the front end
decisions.choice: CSV export for sharing/printing
decisions.WHY: Legacy Q4 agreement; covers the spreadsheet/CSV consumer actor.

decisions.topic: Status engine rules in the rebuild
decisions.choice: Fixed rules: Danger = ANY unpaid past month (not just previous month); Completed overrides Danger when months paid >= tenure; zero-value = unpaid preserved
decisions.WHY: VBA quirk: single-month Danger check hides older misses. Owner-visible correctness win, already agreed in legacy decision summary.

options: Add company once in Watch List (single bonds master), auto-appears in grid/dashboard
Separate entry per sheet like the legacy workbook
decisions.choice: ONE bonds master row per position: user adds the company/position once via the Watch List add form (fields: company, ISIN, amount, tenure, start month); the monthly grid, dashboard, and watch list all render from that same row - details are never entered twice.
decisions.WHY: User requirement 2026-10-30 Q1: 'no need to add two times about the companies and company details'. Closes the gap that no FR covered an add-company flow (legacy XLSM duplicated the same 15 bonds across two sheets; DATA-01 single master kills that).

decisions.topic: Strict active-position lock (same company cannot be bought twice while active)
options: Hard block: key = normalized company name OR ISIN, no override
decisions.choice: At most ONE active (On-going or Danger) position per company. Match key: normalized company name (trim/case-insensitive) OR ISIN - a duplicate is blocked if EITHER matches. Enforcement: HARD BLOCK with a named error naming the active position and its status (FR-21 error surfacing) - no override, no force. The lock releases ONLY when the existing position reaches Completed (D5: months paid >= tenure). A new position bought after Completed starts On-going and re-locks the company until it too completes.
decisions.WHY: User requirement 2026-10-30 Q2: 'same company cannot buy two times while ongoing and in the danger. But if it was completed then it can buy another... very strict locking mechanism.' Pairs with FR-17 reinvestment (Completed frees both capital AND the slot). User chose both company+ISIN keying and hard block over the alternatives.

decisions.topic: Sole entry point + entry-time lock enforcement
options: Watch List add form is the ONLY position entry; D15 lock checked at that submit; grid/dashboard have no add path
decisions.choice: Positions are created ONLY through the Watch List add form. The D15 active-position lock fires at that submit; if blocked, nothing enters the system, so the monthly grid/dashboard can never show a bypassed company. Grid = payment entry + render only; no alternate add route anywhere.
decisions.WHY: User 2026-10-30 Q1: block everything from the watch list itself so nobody can 'easily add in the monthly grid'.

decisions.choice: Rename 'Home Plan' to 'Financial Goals'. Goal entries gain target amount + target end date so 10-year futuristic savings plans are first-class; legacy irregular savings rows (39588/10063/0) import as goals. Tab label: 'Financial Goals'.
decisions.WHY: User Q2 asked for community-checked naming. Research (Savi/Qapital/Mint/OnePay/NerdWallet) shows 'Savings Goal' is the standard term; user explicitly chose 'Financial Goals' from the offered list as the broader umbrella.

decisions.choice: Share panel with per-section checkboxes (totals, per-bond list, monthly history, amounts visibility) generating an offline shareable snapshot: print-styled HTML file + CSV option. Respects privacy mode (amounts masked when hidden). No server, no accounts.
decisions.WHY: User Q3: share investment plan with friends, customizable what to include. User chose customizable snapshot; cloud link rejected as offline-breaking.

options: Global toggle masking all monetary values
decisions.choice: Global 'Privacy Mode' toggle (eye icon in header): masks EVERY monetary value across dashboard, grid, watch list, goals, share snapshot and print as '••••' until toggled back; state persisted locally (browser storage). Numbers, statuses, names stay visible.
decisions.WHY: User Q4: money app must not show amounts on open. Community check: Zerodha 'Privacy Mode' (Kite, Aug 2024) does exactly this - one toggle hides dashboard/holdings/positions/funds values, for focus + showing screens to others. Pattern copied directly.

decisions.choice: Monthly grid rows always sort: Danger first, then On-going, then Completed last; ordering recomputes automatically whenever a status changes (Completed sinks to bottom without user action).
decisions.WHY: User Q5 explicit.

decisions.choice: Dashboard gains a charts row: (1) grouped bars - invested vs received per bond; (2) cumulative returns line - turns red if overall balance goes negative; (3) status donut - Danger/On-going/Completed split. Rendered as inline SVG (no external chart CDN, offline).
decisions.WHY: User Q6 asked for invest/return/negative visualization + community check. Research: line = trend gold standard; grouped columns = invested-vs-received comparison; red/green negative convention (Syncfusion/finance-alliance). User chose full trio.

options: Credit-day daily sweep + Gmail SMTP personal-to-personal
decisions.choice: Status upgrade from month-end to DAY-WISE: each position carries a credit day (day-of-month, from D26); a daily sweep checks that day's payment - unpaid after the credit day -> position flips to Danger immediately. Alerting: in-app notification bell + email sent personal-to-personal via the owner's Gmail SMTP (App Password), one-time user setup; reminder cadence before-due/day-of/overdue per community best practice. Completed logic (D5) unchanged.
decisions.WHY: User Q7 explicit. Research: scheduled daily reminder automation + Python smtplib Gmail App Password is the standard personal-mail path; cloud push/SMS rejected (offline rule, see D24).
decisions.source: user 2026-10-30 Q7 + community (reminder automation best practices)

decisions.choice: Monthly History table shows ONLY elapsed months up to and including the current month; future columns are never rendered; each new month auto-appends its column from the ledger (no headers stored, no future window).
decisions.WHY: User Q8: Excel showed futuristic years; application should not. Auto-append current month each month.

options: In-app + email now; SMS/WhatsApp/push documented as future
decisions.choice: Ship with in-app notification bell + email (per D22). Community-checked alternatives recorded and DEFERRED: SMS/WhatsApp (~98% open but paid cloud), web/mobile push (needs server - breaks offline). Alert history retained in-app (list + timestamps) so the 'strict alert mechanism' is auditable.
decisions.WHY: User Q9: strict alert mechanism + community check other channels. Research (CleverTap/OneSignal/Route Mobile): channels ranked; offline rule decides in-app+email now.

decisions.choice: Deliver a dedicated 'Monthly Print' frontend design: A4 print-optimized HTML showing month header, portfolio summary, this-month payment table, status list, alerts footer; privacy-mode aware (masks if active); approved like the other HTML designs.
decisions.WHY: User Q10 wants to SEE how the monthly print looks before build.

decisions.topic: Add Position upgrade: exact dates + credit day
options: Start date + end date (exact) + credit day
decisions.choice: Add Position form upgraded: exact START DATE and END DATE (date pickers) -> tenure months auto-calculated from the range (no manual tenure). PLUS separate 'Payment credit day' field (day-of-month 1-28) stored per position - this is the date used by the day-wise sweep (D22) and all alert timing (D34). Legacy import maps start_month -> start date, tenure -> computed end date, default credit day = start date's day.
decisions.WHY: User Q11 explicit: exact dates, auto tenure, credit day drives alerts.

options: Start build now on desktop local web app (waves W0-W7)

decisions.topic: MCP server for the application database
options: Deferred READ-ONLY MCP entry for data/bonds.db
decisions.choice: Register deferred MCP server 'sqlite-app-data' in ~/.kimi-code/mcp.json with validated read-only SQLAlchemy URL (sqlite:///file:<abs>/data/bonds.db?mode=ro&uri=true) — agents can SELECT/query bond data (bonds, ledger, goals, notifications) but writes are blocked at the SQLite layer (proven: DELETE -> OperationalError). Doc-store MCP (sqlite-excel-dashboard) stays separate. Shipping an MCP INSIDE the product for friends = future feature, not in this build.
decisions.WHY: User Q 2026-10-30 'shall we add MCP' + 'Q1, add'. Read-only + deferred chosen for financial-data safety (privacy-mode bypass concern documented: MCP exposes amounts to agent sessions on this machine; local-only, no network).

decisions.choice: Project MCP servers (sqlite-app-data + sqlite-excel-dashboard) live ONLY in the project-local .kimi-code/mcp.json of THIS repository; both removed from the global ~/.kimi-code/mcp.json, which now holds only general tools (tavily, brave). decisions.topic: Screen restructure: Portfolio (renamed) + Watchlist = candidates only
decisions.choice: Sidebar: Dashboard | PORTFOLIO (renamed from Month Grid) | WATCHLIST | Financial Goals | Alerts | Settings. PORTFOLIO = two tabs: My Holdings (position registry: full fields, drawer, Received+Next Payout columns, payment-health statuses) and Payouts (the month-grid pattern: mark paid/unpaid, colors, auto-sort Danger top -> Matured bottom). WATCHLIST = candidates only (research list, status 'Watching', Move to Portfolio action; NO invested/received/next-payout/health columns). Payment-health statuses (On-going/Danger/Matured) exist ONLY in Portfolio and are derived from the Payouts grid (owner: 'everything need to reflect from the monthly grid').
decisions.WHY: User Q1+Q2 2026-10-31: status confusion (Completed != purchased), holdings belong in monthly grid, two options in Portfolio, rename grid to Portfolio. Community evidence: stocksbrew watchlist-vs-portfolio separation; IndiaBonds/Groww/BondScanner/Grip payout terminology.

options: A: Add Position inside Portfolio>My Holdings (both paths run D15 lock); relabel Returned->Received, Completed->Matured (display only)

Purchase state: Watching/Held; payment health: On-going/Danger/Matured.
decisions.WHY: Design proposals answering owner's Q1 confusions; owner reviewed the clean HTML design v4 and approved all three proposals.

options: A: 3-way theme switcher (System default / Light / Dark) — data-theme attribute + CSS custom properties + prefers-color-scheme fallback + localStorage persistence
C: light/dark plus accent-color theme gallery
decisions.choice: A: ship three themes — System (follows OS), Light (default), Dark. Header switcher + Settings > Appearance section. Implementation: :root light tokens (current v4 palette) + html[data-theme=dark] dark tokens (near-black surfaces #111827-family, desaturated accents, WCAG AA contrast, no pure white/pure black) + @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) applied only when no explicit data-theme; choice saved in localStorage; zero-flash inline script reads stored theme before first paint.
decisions.WHY: Owner directive 2026-10-31: application must have multiple themes. Community: LogRocket (offer OS Default/Dark/Light choice, never force), web.dev + MDN prefers-color-scheme, shadcn/ui token pattern (all colors switch via CSS variables, zero flash), dev.to (persist choice in localStorage), Atmos (dedicated dark palette — avoid pure white and saturated colors, use surface elevation), Digital Silk (WCAG contrast), Eleken (multi-theme products with dark as first-class option).
